evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Calvin asks 'any in particular concerns aside from price that you have about the move at this time' — but this comes after he's already asked 'Did you have like ten minutes' and probing has begun.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises three concerns (flat rate/no hidden fees, furniture protection for wood items, previous mover elevator delays). Calvin follows up on each: furniture wrapping, hourly rate clarity, and confirms he knows the building and does many downtown moves.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Calvin gives a typical range: 'a one bedroom takes about three to four hours... I would probably put you in a cost range around like $770 to 990' and personalizes it to the customer's situation (26th floor with elevator, organized prep, minimal furniture).
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: No explicit ask for the business. Calvin moves directly into confirming the booking on the 31st without asking 'Would you like our help with your move?' — he assumes acceptance and jumps to logistics.

top_strength: Calvin gathered comprehensive logistics details (floor, elevator proximity, loading dock, truck size fit, item-by-item furniture breakdown, box count) and gave a well-anchored, personalized estimate range with full pricing transparency (hourly rate, minimum, increments, inclusions).
coaching_note: Calvin must ask the explicit close ('Would you like our help with your move?') before assuming acceptance, skip the quid pro quo framing entirely in Section 1, offer the no-worries damage coverage with full terms (no deductible, no fine print, built into rate), and ask a genuine final concerns check in Section 6 rather than the generic 'any other questions.'
booking_note: Customer confirmed move on the 31st with 8:30-9:00 AM start time and provided destination apartment number 2915. Calvin stated 'there's no deposit to book' and will send confirmation email with all details.
